questions.stem: A 35-year-old female presents with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. There is a history of fever and drenching night sweats. She is diagnosed to have Hodgkin's lymphoma. What is the stage of the disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
II-B
  • Involvement of two or more lymph node regions on the same side of the diaphragm alone (II) or localized involvement of an extra-lymphatic organ or site (IIE).
    Presence of (B) symptoms:
  • Unexplained fever,
  • Drenching night sweats, and/or
  • Unexplained weight loss > 10%


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 611-616

questions.stem: Choose the FALSE statement regarding Hodgkin’s lymphoma:

options.label: A
options.text: Affected lymph nodes become painful with alcohol ingestion

options.label: B
options.text: Ann Arbor Stage II is the involvement of two or more lymph node groups on both sides of the diaphragm

options.label: C
options.text: ‘B symptoms’ are fever, night sweats and ≥ 10% weight loss in 6 months

options.label: D
options.text: ABVD regimen is the standard line of treatment

questions.answerText: Ann Arbor Stage II is the involvement of two or more lymph node groups on both sides of the diaphragm
questions.solutionHtml:
Ann Arbor Stage II is the involvement of two or more lymph node groups on both sides of the diaphragm

False, 

  • Ann Arbor Stage II is the involvement of two or more lymph node groups on the same side of the diaphragm.

questions.stem: A person is having painless lymphadenopathy. On biopsy, binucleated owl-shaped nuclei with a clear vacuolated area are seen. On 35-year-old chemistry (IHC) CD 15 and CD 30 were positive. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nodular sclerosis
  • Binucleated owl-shaped nuclei with clear vacuolated area refers to as Lacunar cells.
  • Lacunar cells are seen in the Nodular Sclerosis subtype of Hodgkin’s disease
  • Lacunar cells have delicate, folded, or multilobate nuclei and abundant pale cytoplasm that is often disrupted during the cutting of sections, leaving the nucleus sitting in an empty space (lacuna).


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 611-616

questions.stem: False about nodular lymphocytic predominant Hodgkin’s lymphoma except:

options.label: A
options.text: Consists predominantly of classical RS cells

questions.solutionHtml:
EBV negative

Hodgkin’s Lymphoma:

  • Arises from B cells of the Germinal centre region.
  • Activation of transcription factor NF-κB is a common event in classical Hodgkin’s Lymphoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 611-616

questions.stem: Which cell is not seen in Hodgkin lymphoma -
questions.solutionHtml:
Langerhan cell
  • Langerhans cells are dendritic cells seen in the epidermis of the skin;
  • They act as Antigen-presenting cells.
  • The neoplastic proliferation of Langerhans cells is seen in Langerhans cell Histiocytosis (LCH).
  • Reed Sternberg cell, Lacunar cell, L&H cell (Lymphocytic & Histiocytic variant of Reed- Sternberg cell) & Hodgkin cells are seen in Hodgkin’s disease.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 611-616

questions.stem: A 10 yr old boy with a mass in the abdomen. On imaging, the paraaortic LN is enlarged. On biopsy, a starry sky appearance is seen. What is the underlying abnormality?
questions.solutionHtml:
Translocation involving MYC gene

Burkitt Lymphoma:

  • Burkitt’s has a male predominance and is typically seen in patients <35 years of age.
  • In Burkitt lymphoma, the tumour has a high mitotic index, and numerous apoptotic cells, combined with benign macrophages.
  • Macrophages have abundant clear cytoplasm: a characteristic “starry sky” pattern seen in Lymph Node biopsy.
  • Mutation: C-MYC on Chromosome 8. t (8;14), t (2;8), t (8;22).
  • IHC: CD 10 +, CD19+, CD20+, and BCL6+, surface IgM+
  • Burkitt’s Lymphoma is the most common cause of tumour lysis syndrome.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 601, 602,

questions.stem: Which of the following statements on lymphoma is not True-

options.label: A
options.text: A single classification system for Hodgkin’s disease (HD) is almost universally accepted

options.label: B
options.text: HD more often tends to remain localized to a single group of lymph nodes and spreads by contiguity

options.label: C
options.text: Several types of non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma (NHL) may have a leukemic phase

options.label: D
options.text: In general follicular (nodular) NHL has a worse prognosis compared to diffuse NHL

questions.answerText: In general follicular (nodular) NHL has a worse prognosis compared to diffuse NHL
questions.solutionHtml:
In general follicular (nodular) NHL has a worse prognosis compared to diffuse NHL
  • False, as Follicular Lymphoma is a low-grade Non-Hodgkin’s and has a better prognosis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 611-616

questions.stem: Post-transplant lymphoma occurs due to the proliferation of which of the following cells -
questions.solutionHtml:
B cell
  • Post-transplant lymphoma (Post-transplant Lymphoproliferative Disorder or PTLD) occurs due to the proliferation of B cells, 90% being EBV positive.
